Yes, on both halves of the question, checked by execution rather than reading.

REACHES THE SCORED PREDICTION. The code lands in the last 128 coordinates of every command token (verified: first 640 dims bit-identical to the baseline, delta RMS exactly 1.0 per row, input tensor unmutated, deterministic — scratchpad/t3.py). Those tokens are the model's input at the scored read position: with the genome's own arch (r22) built and trained for 6 steps, zeroing only the code slice of the read command token moved that position's prediction by max|Δ| = 0.360 (scratchpad/t6.py). The instrument reconstructs the same coding per arm (cups_probe.py:168-243) and the impl's collate reproduces code_cmds bit-exactly (collate cmd tokens == code_cmds output: True; obs tokens / tgt / types / key_pad / cmd_mask all bit-identical to baseline_interleave — scratchpad/t3.py). Prefix-causality: 0 violations over every cut of every sampled sequence, i.e. the instrument's own check at cups_probe.py:205-218 cannot fire.

THE SIGNAL IS THE RIGHT SIGN, MEASURED ON THE REAL SLICE. Native arm: the cups_test read's resolved code equals the routed content's expose-step code in 2560/2560 train and 1280/1280 val windows. Role-swapped arm (replaying cups_probe.build_swap_cache's partner selection, seed 20260806): the read's code equals the PARTNER's expose code in 1822/1822 train and 922/922 val windows, and equals the native routed content's code in 0 of them (scratchpad/t10.py). So native_hit and swap_stayed are driven in opposite directions by construction, not in expectation — the hypothesis's central claim (lines 58-66) is exact.

GRADIENT. Cross-entropy of a step's code with the retrieval target is trainable: after 6 real _train steps on the genome, cmd_proj.weight.grad has norm 0.0435 over the 128 code columns vs 0.0572 over the 640 text columns — ~2.6x higher per dimension on the code slice (scratchpad/t6.py). The parent's file memory is exactly the consumer the hypothesis claims: keys k_file = quotient(file_write(x_cmd)), queries q_file = quotient(file_read(x_cmd)), values = obs_tok (r22_retrieval_composition_renderer.py:86-95), read strictly-causally (tril diagonal=-1, r18_pathstate_latent_transition_worldmodel.py:208). And the retrieval target really is the answer: the read step's z_obs is BIT-IDENTICAL to the routed expose step's z_obs in 402/402 val windows checked against the actual embedding cache (min cos 0.9999996) — so "returns the expose step's observation embedding, which is bit-for-bit the target" is literally true.

COST. Memoization works as claimed: 0.82 ms/sequence cold, 0.0084 ms/sequence warm (≈0.54 ms per bs=64 step). The 20,000-entry cache never thrashes on this root (2,560 train sequences).

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. (a) Whether CODE_SCALE=1.0 is large enough for the learned projections to isolate the code from the 640 residual text dimensions — the author flags this as the primary unhedged risk and it is genuinely only answerable by a full scored run. (b) The blend composition of the actual TWM_TRAIN_ROOT: all data measurements above are on data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd, the only encoded root available locally. The two coverage gaps below (bare relative filenames) are inert on that root but I cannot rule them out for other packs in a blend. (c) Failure-mode 2 (SNR cost on non-cups packs) — unmeasurable without a run.
summary:
The code does what the hypothesis says it does, and the load-bearing claims are exact rather than approximate. I verified by execution against the real pack: the resolver's mv/cp/rm/`>`/`>>`/cd semantics all behave as specified; the code is a zero-mean, unit-RMS 128-d vector added only to the last 128 of 768 command coordinates; collate and code_cmds agree bit-for-bit and everything else (observation tokens, tgt, types, key_pad, cmd_mask, even-index extraction, CUPS_LAYOUT) is bit-identical to the baseline stream; code_cmds is prefix-causal with zero violations over every cut of every sampled sequence; and there were ZERO false matches — 10,063 code repeats across 113,722 train+val steps, every single one landing on a step with an identical rendered observation.

The two claims that decide the score are exact, not statistical. Native arm: the read's resolved code equals the routed content's expose code in 2560/2560 train and 1280/1280 val windows. Role-swapped arm (replaying the instrument's own partner selection): the read's code equals the PARTNER's expose code in 1822/1822 and 922/922 windows, and the native routed content's code in zero. And the retrieval target is genuinely reachable: the read step's z_obs is bit-identical to the routed expose step's z_obs in 402/402 val windows checked against the real embedding cache.

The five divergences I found are all in peripheral rationale or in regimes this data never produces: the "ordinary steps train the copy pathway" claim is mis-attributed (98% of the matching-code steps are the cvar_test/cups_test probe reads themselves, though the ~9%-of-steps frequency the argument rests on does hold); bare slash-free relative filenames are neither normalized by `cd` nor epoch-poisoned when mutated, which can manufacture a false match in principle but occurs 0 times in 113,722 steps here; the observation render carries no cwd under the pinned eye, contra the stated justification; and "exactly when"/"9%" are small overstatements (7.79%). None of them touch the scored path.

THE ONE THING THE ARCHIVE RECORD MUST CARRY, which is not a divergence because the hypothesis states it plainly (lines 15-41): this stream solves the routing SYMBOLICALLY, outside the network. It parses the command strings, maintains a points-to table, and hands the read command a token that already carries the exact identity of the content sitting at the read location. The network's remaining job is to learn "retrieve the earlier observation whose command token shares my code" — not to learn routing. This is inside the stream contract (code_cmds exists precisely so a stream may write into command tokens, the instrument reproduces it per arm, it is prefix-causal, and nothing in it is specific to the eval images, so it transfers to unseen systems). But comp_ca for this candidate measures the net's ability to exploit an exact hand-computed address, and a reader who sees only the number will not know that. That belongs in the archived note.

divergences.claim: "any repeated read anywhere in training (`cat P` twice, `ls /d` twice with nothing written to /d in between) also gets a matching code, so the copy pathway is trained by a large fraction of ordinary steps rather than by the rare deep windows" (hypothesis.txt:54-57)
divergences.what_the_code_does: The mechanism does give repeated reads a matching code, but on the real training split almost none of those repeats are ordinary steps. Over all 2560 train sequences (75,832 steps) 6,715 steps (8.9%) carry a code that matches an earlier step in the same sequence — and 6,576 of them (98%) are cvar_test (4,016) or cups_test (2,560) capability-probe reads. Ordinary steps contribute 139 matches total (role 'read' 130, 'cups_ctx' 9), i.e. 0.18% of steps. The operative frequency claim (~9% of positions, not a rare deep window) survives; the attribution to 'ordinary steps' does not.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/t11.py over data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/train.jsonl → role/steps/code-matches-earlier: cvar_expose 13952/0, cups 12856/0, read 11548/130, cvar_op 11088/0, cups_expose 8826/0, cvar_test 7776/4016, cups_ctx 3604/9, cwd_anchor 2560/0, cups_test 2560/2560, cvar_read 1062/0; TOTAL 75832/6715

divergences.claim: "`cd` : tracks cwd, so relative paths normalize" (hypothesis.txt:25)
divergences.what_the_code_does: cwd is tracked correctly, but _is_path(t) (stream__alias_resolved_content_codes.py:65-68) requires a '/' in the token, so a bare relative filename is never treated as a path and is never normalized against cwd. `cd /a; cat f` keys as the literal token 'f', while `cat /a/f` keys as the resolved identity 'p:0:/a/f' — the two do not match. Relative paths normalize only when they contain a slash ('./f', 'sub/f', '../f'), which do work.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/t7.py / t8.py: `cd /a; cat ./f` vs `cat /a/f` → keys equal (True); `cd /a; cat sub/f` vs `cat /a/sub/f` → True; `cd /a; cat f` vs `cat /a/f` → False, keys 'cwd=/a\x1fcat\x1ff' vs 'cwd=/a\x1fcat\x1fp:0:/a/f'. Inert on this pack: 0 `cd` commands and 0 mutating commands with a bare-name argument in 113,722 train+val steps (scratchpad/t9.py).

divergences.claim: "any shell form it cannot parse (pipe, glob, quoting, $, backtick) that also mutates: it increments an epoch that poisons every subsequent untracked identity, so a stale identity can never produce a false match." (hypothesis.txt:26-28)
divergences.what_the_code_does: The epoch guard only fires on the _OPAQUE_TOKENS/_OPAQUE_CHARS detector (lines 146-150). A mutation whose verb parses but whose arguments are bare slash-free names — `mv f g`, `cp f g` — is neither opaque nor resolvable: the mv/cp branch's arg check fails (line 183) and it falls through to the generic _MUT_VERBS loop (lines 201-207), which finds no _is_path argument, updates nothing, and does NOT bump the epoch. A later `cat g` therefore reuses the literal key it had before the move, producing a confident false match — the exact outcome the epoch mechanism is claimed to make impossible. (Note also: the opaque branch additionally does loc.clear(), which the hypothesis does not mention; without the clear, the epoch bump alone would not poison already-tracked identities, since tracked values carry no epoch. So the implemented guard is safer than described, but its trigger condition is narrower than described.)
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/t8.py: ["cat g", "mv f g", "cat g"] → key[0]==key[2] is True, epoch=0, both 'cwd=/\x1fcat\x1fg' — same code, different content. Same for `cp f g`. Absolute-path control ["cat /d/g","mv /d/f /d/g","cat /d/g"] correctly gives False. Severity held to minor because scratchpad/t9.py finds 0 mutating-verb-with-bare-argument steps in both splits of the local pack (75,832 + 37,890 steps); it would become material if the blended TWM_TRAIN_ROOT includes a pack that uses relative-path mutations.

divergences.claim: "plus the current cwd (the observation text contains cwd, so cwd belongs in the key)" (hypothesis.txt:31) and "The `mv` steps produce an EMPTY observation (\"cwd=/ exit=0\\n\")" (hypothesis.txt:5-6)
divergences.what_the_code_does:
Under the pinned eye the observation render carries no cwd: evolve/chunks/perception/enc_e5_base_nocwd.py:5-8 renders "passage: exit=<n>
<output>", and enc_e5_ft_nocwd_hf.py re-exports it. So the stated justification for putting cwd in the key is false, and the mv observation is "passage: exit=0
", not "cwd=/ exit=0
". No behavioral consequence on this pack: cwd is constant within a sequence (only '/' and '/data' appear, and there are no `cd` commands), so a cwd term can never split a within-sequence match here.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/perception/enc_e5_base_nocwd.py:5-8; evolve/chunks/perception/enc_e5_ft_nocwd_hf.py:2. cwd distribution over the jail sample: {'/' : 634, '/data': 90}, verbs {cat, mv, ls} only — no `cd`.

divergences.claim: "Two commands carry the same code exactly when they read the same content" (hypothesis.txt:41) and "roughly a 9% token-norm increase" (hypothesis.txt:45)
divergences.what_the_code_does: The forward direction is verified exactly (same code ⇒ same rendered observation, 0 counterexamples in 10,063 code repeats across both splits), but 'exactly when' is not an iff: `cat P` and `head P` over the same content, or two distinct untouched files holding equal bytes, get different codes by construction. The measured token-norm increase is 7.79%, not 9%.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/t10.py: train 75,832 steps / 6,715 code repeats / 0 false matches; val 37,890 steps / 3,348 repeats / 0 false matches. scratchpad/t3.py: norm ratio 1.0779 (= sqrt(896/768)).
